nodes.label: Research-to-customer-support i18n key rename
nodes.norm_label: research mode to customer support key rename
nodes.summary: Reused id. The user asked for the statistics tab to stop being called Research and read Customer Support, including the group tag hint and sidebar badge. Verified by parent grep: zero occurrences of research/riset in either locale file afterwards, key contract test 42/42 at exit 0.

nodes.label: Rename stops at persisted contract; visible copy only
nodes.norm_label: rename stops at persisted contract
nodes.summary: research_mode_enabled (preference key), research_tag (DB column), set_research_tag_cmd (CLI-facing) and the RESEARCH_* error strings are left named for research. Only tab label, tab id, the 40 en/id strings, the group badge and the modal hint change. Repeated at the end: the renamed-everything promise is deliberately narrower than it sounds.

nodes.label: One round trip replaces a serial mode gate, with a per-field degrade contract
nodes.norm_label: single round trip command with partial failure degrade
nodes.summary: get_customer_support_overview returns mode, days, active_days, csat: Option<CsatSummary>, recent_conversations and snippets in one call. A failed CSAT aggregate sets that one field to null and the trend still renders; export moved to a separate command wired only at the click handler.

nodes.label: Freeze the cross-chunk contract before dispatching the fan-out
nodes.norm_label: frozen cross chunk contract before fanout
nodes.summary: The tab chunk needs i18n keys, the chart component and backend command names that other chunks own. The parent writes the exact key names, values, command names, struct fields and props into the manifest first, so every chunk codes against a frozen contract instead of waiting on a sibling. One documented ordering constraint survived: the i18n chunk lands first because the rest verify against its keys.

nodes.label: Test files left unowned by the manifest block the audit gate
nodes.norm_label: unowned test files block the audit gate
nodes.summary: GroupModal.test.tsx, SnippetsSidebar.test.tsx, ResearchModeToggle.test.tsx and StatisticsPage.test.tsx assert the old key names but no chunk was permitted to edit them, so the gate would have been blocked on red assertions nobody could fix. Fixed by re-chunking as one follow-up rather than loosening scope.

nodes.label: An SVG chart must ship a screen-reader-reachable data table
nodes.norm_label: svg chart requires screen reader data table
nodes.summary: Two primary sources, W3C WAI Complex Images and USWDS Data visualizations, land on the same requirement: the SVG is aria-hidden with an sr-only data table as the accessible equivalent, using a clip-based visually-hidden pattern rather than display:none. Parent-verified after the fact that no display:none sits on the table.

nodes.label: Already-hashed source id must not be hashed again on submit
nodes.norm_label: prehashed source id avoids double hash
nodes.summary: analytics_events.source_id is already an opaque hashed id, so feeding it back through submit_csat_response would hash it twice. Resolved with a second command submit_csat_for_source that records the already-opaque value, keeping each command with one clear contract instead of a double-hash bug.

nodes.label: Deep-link tab gate silently falls back to overview
nodes.norm_label: deep link tab gate silently falls back
nodes.summary: resolveRequestedTab validates against VALID_STATISTICS_TABS and silently falls back to "overview" on a miss. Leaving "research" in that list would let requestStatisticsTab("customer_support") typecheck while being rejected at runtime, making the renamed tab unreachable by deep link and looking correct to the type checker. Found by a subagent widening scope; the parent verified the claim before accepting it.

nodes.label: Absence inferred from one naming convention is not evidence
nodes.norm_label: absence from narrow grep is not evidence
nodes.summary: The parent claimed a Rust subagent had skipped its tests on the strength of a grep for fn test_ returning 13. The seven tests were on disk at lines 1152-1357, named without the prefix. The subagent that had been re-dispatched to write them corrected the parent, and a chunk was dispatched for work that already existed. Stated as: infer absence from a search matching only one convention, then act on it, is the defect.

nodes.label: Parent re-verifies each subagent report instead of trusting the self-report
nodes.norm_label: parent verifies subagent reports independently
nodes.summary: All ten reports were re-checked in the parent: the deep-link gate claim, the dead CSS class, the Unicode watch item, the chart accessibility properties, the silent refresh flag. The verification found four real problems including two wrong causal claims in the reports themselves, and the session states plainly that the elapsed time was partly this cost.

nodes.label: Derive is transitive, so adding Debug to one struct widens the database layer
nodes.norm_label: debug derive transitivity forces layer widening
nodes.summary: A test used {:?} on Vec<SupportConversationCandidate>, which does not compile because the struct derives Serialize and not Debug. Adding Debug to all four new structs for consistency then demanded Debug on ResearchDayRow and CsatSummary, which live in the database layer this change deliberately does not touch. Corrected to derive on only the two leaf structs the failing assertion formats.

nodes.label: Byte-equivalence test pins an extracted serializer
nodes.norm_label: byte equivalence test pins serializer refactor
nodes.summary: serialize_research_rows was extracted so both the old and new export commands share it, and get_research_export was reduced to a byte-identical 4-line delegation. test_export_customer_support_report_matches_get_research_export is what actually proves the shared serializer did not change the JSON or CSV output format, and it only runs on the VPS.

nodes.label: Bar density defect found only by rendering, not by DOM assertions
nodes.norm_label: chart bar density defect found only by rendering
nodes.summary: 12/12 DOM tests, a clean typecheck and parent re-inspection all passed while the chart was unusable: rendering to static SVG and measuring showed 162 bars at 1.07px on a 720px plot, with axis labels clustered at the right edge and the final day labelled as if it were a boundary. A chart of hairline bars is still the raw-looking view the user complained about.

nodes.label: Bucket ladder for long date ranges with a 3px bar floor
nodes.norm_label: chart bucket ladder for long ranges
nodes.summary: The fix buckets rather than drops: on an 81-day range 81 crowded bars became 12 buckets, narrowest bar went 1.07px to 16px, labels sit at even 110-unit spacing and the last day is no longer labelled. 3px is now a hard floor that holds at every range, short ranges still render per-day bars, and the accessible table describes the buckets actually drawn.

nodes.label: i18n literal guard matches a > followed by a capitalised identifier
nodes.norm_label: i18n guard matches arrow function gt
nodes.summary: The completeness guard flags a capitalised word of 7+ characters and therefore matches the > of an arrow function followed by capitalised code, as in > BUCKET_DAY_STEPS.find(...). It also matches inside comments. Reformatting did not clear it and neither did removing the arrow until the expression was rewritten without one. Same false-positive class as the ASCII-only character class defect.

nodes.label: Duplicate i18n keys shadow keys the codebase already shares
nodes.norm_label: duplicate i18n keys shadow shared keys
nodes.summary: cancel, save, description and createGroup already exist in main.ts and are used by roughly ten components each. Creating four duplicates was a defect the change itself introduced; the fix was to repoint at the shared keys, which then broke the modal's own tests because their mockT stub still carried the removed duplicates.

nodes.label: Isolated VPS worktree because another session was live-editing
nodes.norm_label: isolated vps worktree for concurrent session
nodes.summary: Reused id. The VPS fast-forward aborted because of the other session's uncommitted work, so rather than stash or checkout files that were not its own, a separate worktree was created at the exact base commit and the other session's dirty tree left untouched.

nodes.label: tauri-build panic trap from empty gitignored resources
nodes.norm_label: tauri build prerequisite provisioning
nodes.summary: Reused id, same claim class. A cold cargo check in the fresh verify worktree panicked in tauri::generate_context! because apps/web/dist did not exist, the same cold-build trap the repo docs already warn about for the CLI sidecar and the Whisper model. The sidecar and the byte-verified model were provisioned in advance precisely to avoid it.

nodes.label: Running the installed desktop binary with --version launches a GUI instance
nodes.norm_label: version flag launches gui instance
nodes.summary: snipset-desktop --version to compare versions started a full GUI process instead of printing a version, collided with the live app on the control API port (Address already in use), and left a second PID behind. It exited on its own; the pre-existing instance was never at risk and no stray process remained.

nodes.label: pgrep matching its own command line reports a false RUNNING
nodes.norm_label: pgrep self match false running signal
nodes.summary: Two self-inflicted process errors that would both have read as compile results: a pgrep that matched the ssh command line containing the pattern and reported RUNNING with no cargo process alive, and a pkill on the same command line as the launch that killed the shell before the launch happened.

nodes.label: Merge verified by content because the merge rebased
nodes.norm_label: verify merge by content not sha ancestry
nodes.summary: Reused id. The pushed commit dd42b4148 was not found in origin/main, and the assistant refused to guess why. Checking content settled it: four CustomerSupport files present, ResearchStatisticsTab gone, and the two commits rebased to cba7aa647 and 92d358a3c, so the SHAs changed while the content landed whole.

nodes.label: Persisted identifiers are renamed only with a migration and CLI parity work
nodes.norm_label: rename stops at persisted contract
nodes.summary: Stated in the note's own words: research_mode_enabled, research_tag, set_research_tag_cmd and the RESEARCH_* error strings are persisted contract, and renaming those needs a migration plus CLI parity work, so they stay.

nodes.label: A slow mode check gated the whole tab and one rejection blanked everything
nodes.norm_label: one round trip replaces serial mode gate
nodes.summary: The old code fired get_research_mode, then only if true fired a Promise.all of two more, so a slow mode check gated the entire tab and any single rejection blanked everything. CSAT, ticket ref and snippet UUID were three hand-typed text inputs on top of that.

nodes.label: Freeze the contract so a chunk never waits on a sibling
nodes.norm_label: frozen contract so chunks never block
nodes.summary: Stated directly: now let me freeze the shared contract before fanning out, so chunks never block on each other. The tab chunk depends on keys, the chart and command names owned by other chunks, and a red chunk could otherwise not be verified in isolation.

nodes.label: Red for a reason that is not a product defect still blocks the gate
nodes.norm_label: test files asserting renamed keys need an owner
nodes.summary: The stated reason for re-chunking rather than absorbing: four test files that assert the old key names now have no owner, which means the audit gate would be blocked on red assertions nobody is allowed to fix. That is a manifest gap, and the fix is a re-chunk, not a reason to loosen scope.

nodes.label: The data table is the accessible equivalent both sources require, not a nice-to-have
nodes.norm_label: accessible table required not optional
nodes.summary: Read in full via TinyFish from W3C WAI Complex Images and the USWDS data-visualization guidance: the chart's accessibility is not a style preference. That is why the exact-numbers view stays, and why it uses a clip-based visually-hidden pattern rather than display:none.

nodes.label: Re-hashing an already opaque id is harmless but semantically sloppy
nodes.summary: Two commands is ugly, but each has a clear contract and no double-hash bug, which is recorded as an explicit decision rather than left implicit.
nodes.norm_label: prehashed ref not rehashed

nodes.label: A search matching one naming convention is not a search for the tests
nodes.norm_label: narrow grep cannot prove absence
nodes.summary: The parent states the correction as its own error: the probe was the defect, not the subagent. Inferred absence from a search that only matched one naming convention, then re-dispatched a chunk to write tests that already existed.

nodes.label: rustfmt --check was clean and would never have found the derive error
nodes.norm_label: rustfmt clean but compiler found derive error
nodes.summary: The note offers this as the whole argument for the mandatory VPS compile: the derive error was found by cargo and nothing else, and the same error class is exactly what a green frontend suite says nothing about.

nodes.label: A refactor with no equivalence test is the shape of a silent regression
nodes.norm_label: equivalence test because refactor changes bytes
nodes.summary: The export must produce byte-identical JSON and CSV to the existing command. Without that test, if the shared serializer changed the CSV format, nothing would catch it.

nodes.label: Rendering 162 hairline bars does not fix a view that reads raw
nodes.norm_label: render to measure because dom cannot measure
nodes.summary: The whole premise of the task is that this chart fixes a view that reads raw, so the measured geometry is the acceptance criterion, not the passing DOM assertions. Stated as I am not shipping that as verified.

nodes.label: Four duplicate keys make the codebase worse, not better
nodes.norm_label: shared i18n keys already used by ten components
nodes.summary: cancel, save, description and createGroup already exist and are used by roughly ten components each, so creating duplicates was a real defect introduced by this change. The subagent reporting the collision was right, and the fix was to repoint rather than accept.

nodes.label: Another session's uncommitted files are not mine to stash or check out
nodes.norm_label: isolated worktree over stashing another session
nodes.summary: The fast-forward aborted on the other session's uncommitted work. Since only two files needed typechecking and they were identical across the two commits apart from its own edits, a separate worktree at the exact base commit was the clean approach, leaving the dirty tree untouched.

nodes.label: Content equality proves the work landed where ancestry cannot
nodes.norm_label: verify merged content not sha ancestry
nodes.summary: Reused id. The pushed SHA was absent from origin/main and the note declined to guess the cause, checking main's contents instead and finding the squash-or-rebase explanation consistent with the files being present.
